'''Krevinian''', or '''Krevin''' ({{langx|lv|krieviņu dialekts}}) was a dialect of the [[Votic language]], spoken in Latvia until the mid-19th century.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/universalgeogra13maltgoog|title=Universal Geography: Or A Description of All Parts of the World, on a New Plan, According to the Great Natural Divisions of the Globe|last=Malte-Brun|first=Conrad|date=1829|publisher=A. Finley|pages=[https://archive.org/details/universalgeogra13maltgoog/page/n80 64]|language=en}}</ref> It was spoken in the city of [[Bauske]], in [[Courland]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WubvXTkjoLUC&pg=PA11|title=An Introduction to the Uralic Languages|last=Collinder|first=Björn|date=1975|publisher=University of California Press|pages=11|language=en}}</ref>

The Krevinian dialect left loanwords into the Bauska dialects, such as {{lang|lt|kurika}} 'cudgel'.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rajavuori|first=Anna|date=2014-04-12|title=Seminaariraportti: Performatiivista kulttuuria ja poliittisia performansseja|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.30666/elore.79129|journal=Elore|volume=21|issue=1|doi=10.30666/elore.79129|issn=1456-3010|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Sample ==
{{Poem quote|text={{lang|zkv|Meģģi ise taiwâs!
jadku elka śiwu śenna
tulap meģģi tiwi śivu riikki!
Śiwu meelle se iggau ka kui taiwâs ni kans ma bēli!
Meģģi arma leipe anna meli tennawa.
Ġedde meggi padudd, kui me jattim umili nisi meli jad!
Elas meite kurja sad.
Śewon wodse kurģe miusse erre
Jo siula kalpap śiwu kikki śiwu appi un śiwu üwiwi śewonśe śewonśe.
Amen}}
|title=The Lord's prayer in Krevinian|source=<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ernits|first=Enn|title=Ein neuer rekonstruktionsversuch der kreewinischen texte}}</ref>}}
